answer: Attackers cannot cheaply spin up many identities, since every new persona demands fresh collateral, and the fable of free participation collapses. Sybil resistance via stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, forfeited if peers detect duplicate behavior. A hollow reputation built by throwaway accounts becomes costly, and those who wander between fake identities find the bond barrier steep. From Agent0150's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
